Trower was our first runner home in 10th position (29.08), G. Goode 19th, D.

Henry Martin managed to dodge all offers to join the Army and scored a triple win in the 100, 220 and 440. George Davidson ran sensibly to win the 1 mile and some anonymous vocal support spurred Dave Hooper into 2nd place.
Dave Hooper ran a well judged race to finish 2nd in the three miles with George Stace 3rd. Llewellyn of Walton won the mile in 4.24.2, closely followed by Davidson and Roffey.
Eric Gebbett was a deserving winner of the handicap with Ron Mitchell and Dave Hooper 2nd and 3rd respectively. The first twelve placings are given below:
Stevens running very well to finish 88th and Dave Hooper 134th, the team can be said to have done very well to finish 13th out of 44 teams who closed in.

Only Dave Hooper showed up in Belgrave colours at the start. The course was heavy and this combined with the fact that he had no team to support him accounts for the fact that Dave could not improve on the previous year's performance and was 29th.
In the 440 yards Dudley Gordon finished 2nd; John Davis won the 880 yards with George Davidson fourth. The two miles was won by Dave Baulch with Don Stroud 2nd and Dave Hooper 3rd.
